title: It’s a thermos that calls itself a food jar with a great folding spoon; instructiions are poor
text:
It’s a thermos that calls itself a food jar with a great folding spoon; instructiions are poor. I am almost sorry I purchased this based on the other five-star reviews. First of all, this appears to be like any other thermos. The poorly-written instructions say this is a food jar with the ability to "cook" food inside. However, anything that is hard to cook, needs to be cooked first before putting into this "jar."

This unit comes in four parts that includes the base reservoir, the interior sealing lid with a foldable stainless steel spoon, and the top lid that can double as a soup cup. It also comes with an insulated carry bag and poorly written instructions such as "How to smoldering the food."

I pre-heated the thermos with boiling water as instructed and waited 10 minutes. I them dumped the water and put in my grains and added the necessary boiling water. I then sealed both caps, put it in the insulated bag, and by morning I had softened grains in cool water. I had to heat them to cook them.

Now it does say hard cooking grains should be cooked on the stove first but I chose to do it last. Even though the grains softened, I took issue with the fact that I had cool water by the morning. If this is insulated, I would have expected the water to be at least warm and it was not. Perhaps it cooled faster because I did not fill the water to the tippy top. Therefore, I did a test with a full container of boiling water. After nine hours the water was warm and by morning it was cool again, although not as cool as it was when I did not fill it to the top. Therefore, it keeps things hot for about four hours, warm for about eight, and cooler after that.

The best thing about this is the spoon. The spoon does need to be about one inch longer to easily get to the bottom of the thermos, but it still is a nice touch.

For those that care, this cannot be put in the dishwasher.

In summary, I can use this as a thermos for short stints but I will not be "cooking" with this. It certainly can be used to soften beans and grains before cooking if desired. It is perfect for storing loose leaf tea which is what I use some small thermoses for because they are airtight and keep out the light that destroys tea. This thermos would also have been better if it had a handle around the side. It is a little wide and somewhat hard for me to wrap my hand around the girth. If one is filling this to the brim with liquid, then it will stay warm to hot longer.
